question: How Does Subscription Syncing to a Specific Date Work?
metaDescription: Subscription syncing bills every customer on the same fixed date instead of their signup anniversary — how it works, and how the first prorated charge behaves.
shortAnswer: Subscription syncing (enabled per product under Product data → Subscription → Synchronise renewals) bills every customer on the same fixed date — the 1st of the month, for example — instead of on the anniversary of when each individual customer signed up. A customer joining partway through the cycle is charged a prorated amount up front for the partial period, then moves onto the shared billing date from that point on.

bodyHtml:
How It Works

Without syncing, each subscription bills on its own anniversary — a customer who signs up on the 14th gets charged on the 14th of every following period. With syncing enabled on the product, everyone is instead billed on the same calendar date, which is common for businesses that want predictable, batched billing (and simpler bookkeeping) rather than charges spread across every day of the month.

A customer who signs up partway through a cycle is charged a prorated amount covering just the days between signup and the next shared billing date, so they aren't overcharged for a period they didn't fully use before joining the synced schedule.

Common Points of Confusion

  • Customers questioning the prorated first charge, which is often a smaller, unfamiliar-looking amount compared to the regular recurring price — worth explaining clearly at checkout, since it's easy to mistake for a billing error.
  • Syncing only applies going forward from when it's enabled — existing subscriptions created before syncing was turned on don't automatically move onto the new shared date unless explicitly migrated.
  • Trial periods interacting with sync dates in ways that need careful testing — a trial plus a sync date means the first real charge timing depends on both settings together, not just one.
  • Sync date configured per-product, not store-wide — different subscription products can have entirely different (or no) sync dates, which is easy to forget when auditing why one product's billing pattern differs from another's.

Setting It Up Correctly

  1. Enable and configure the sync date under the product's Subscription settings, choosing the day of the month (or a specific date, depending on the billing interval) everyone should be charged on.
  2. Test a signup partway through the cycle to confirm the prorated first charge calculates and displays correctly before launching.
  3. Communicate the prorated first-charge behavior clearly at checkout or in a confirmation email, since it's the detail most likely to generate a support question.
  4. For existing subscriptions that need migrating onto a new sync date, that's not automatic and needs a deliberate, tested migration plan rather than just turning the setting on.

See custom WooCommerce development for migrating existing subscriptions onto a synced billing date without disrupting active customers.
